# TDPdf v2.0.0.0

**Three things TDPdf could only pretend to do, it now actually does: redaction that removes the content, text editing that replaces the words, and forms it can create rather than only fill in.**

A major version because the last of those changes what an existing operation *means*. "Edit text" used to leave the original wording in the file. It no longer does.

> **If you are already on 1.30.2.0**, the redaction, text-editing and form-creation code is physically in that build — it shipped without being described. This release is where those capabilities are announced, documented and supported. Everything below the "New in this release" heading is genuinely new.


## Redaction

### Marked content is deleted, not covered

The objects under a mark are removed from the page and the content stream is rebuilt around their absence. Document metadata is cleared at the same time — redacting a name from the body while leaving it in the Title is the classic miss.

Every redaction is then **verified on the finished file**. If any text still sits inside an area you redacted, the save fails and no file is written. A tool that hands back a document that merely looks safe is worse than one that refuses, so this one refuses.

Text hidden inside embedded objects is removed too. That is where a scanned page keeps its invisible OCR layer, which is exactly the document people most want to redact.

### The Redact tool

`R`, or the red block in the toolbar. Drag over anything to mark it, click a mark to take it back off, then press **Redact Permanently**.

Marks are dashed red outlines, not solid black boxes, on purpose: a pending mark that already looks finished invites printing or sending a document whose content is entirely still there. Nothing is removed until you apply, and applying says plainly that it cannot be undone. Saving with marks still pending asks first, because a mark is not a redaction.

### Redact every match of a search

Find a name, press **Redact matches**, and every occurrence in the document is marked — including on pages you have never scrolled to.

It stops at marking, deliberately. A search match is not a decision: "Smith" finds the name being removed and the Smith who signed the letter. The marks are ordinary marks, so you can click any one of them off before pressing **Redact Permanently**.

### Scanned pages can be redacted

A scan is one page-sized image, so there is no object to delete — deleting "the object the name is in" would delete the entire page. TDPdf now offers to replace such a page with an image of itself with the marked areas painted out, which removes the content completely.

It is always offered, never silent, because it costs the page its text: a rasterised page can no longer be searched, selected, copied, or read aloud by a screen reader. Other pages in the same document are redacted normally and keep theirs. The same path handles pages whose content cannot be rewritten safely — spot colour, gradients, inline images, soft masks — which previously had to be refused outright.

## Text editing that changes the document, not a picture of it

Editing existing text used to paint a white rectangle over the old words and draw the new ones on top. The original was still in the file, still selectable, still in every extraction, on every machine the file reached.

The words are now replaced on the text object itself, keeping its font, size and colour, so the edit matches the rest of the line and the old wording is genuinely gone.

Where that is not possible, TDPdf says so rather than guessing. Most PDFs embed only the glyphs the document already used, so a file that never contained a "Z" has no "Z" to draw with. In that case it names the exact characters the font cannot draw and falls back to the old overlay behaviour, rather than silently leaving blanks where the letters should be. The status line always says which of the two happened.

## Form creation

TDPdf could already fill in a PDF form. It can now make one.

The Form tool (`F`) places text boxes, paragraph boxes, check boxes, radio groups, dropdowns and empty signature fields. Drag a box on the page and it is there, fillable immediately and by any other PDF reader. Dropdowns and radio groups ask for their choices; a radio group is drawn as one box and its buttons are spread along it.

While the tool is out, existing fields show as named outlines rather than boxes to type in, so you can see the form you are building and place fields beside the ones already there. Click a field to rename it, mark it required or read-only, or delete it.

Every field carries a real appearance stream, so it shows up in print, in a flattened copy, and in readers that do not generate their own.

## New in this release

### A measurement tool

Press `M`, or pick the ruler in the toolbar, and drag across anything on the page. It reports the distance in **inches, millimetres and PDF points at once** — all three rather than a unit you have to switch, because a ruler is on screen for the few seconds a drag takes to read, and a unit mode is something to discover, get wrong, and re-drag.

It measures the page as the page really is. A page turned a quarter turn, or cropped tighter than the sheet it sits on, reads correctly, and the same drag reports the same number whatever the zoom or the monitor. It touches nothing in the document — it is a readout, not an edit.

### Letter spacing for text boxes

For lining typing up with the boxes on a preprinted form — the thing this app is used for most. Spacing can be negative as well as positive, for a form tighter than the font's natural pitch.

The spacing you set is the spacing that wraps the text, that sizes the box, and that lands in the saved PDF. One honest limit: while you are actually **typing**, the text shows at its natural spacing. The editor Windows gives us cannot draw spacing without putting the cursor and the selection highlight in the wrong places, which would be worse than not showing it. Spacing applies the instant the box commits — and committing is the only moment text can move. Saving never is.

### Duplicate a page

The Pages panel can copy a page, or a whole selection of them. Copies land together after the last page you selected, each keeping its own rotation, and the new copies come up selected and on screen.

### The pointer says what it can do

The Select tool now shows a text cursor only where there is text to select, the hand over a link, and the ordinary arrow on blank page — so it stops promising a selection the page cannot give. Things you can pick up show an open hand that closes while you carry them: placing a signature or a stamp, and dragging a text box by its grip.

### Fixed: dragging pages

Three defects in dragging pages around the Pages panel, all of them in the feature that was supposed to let you move several at once:

- **It did not work unless you happened to be holding Ctrl.** Windows collapses a multi-row selection to the row you pressed on, on the press itself — one gesture before a drag starts. So by the time you had moved far enough to drag, the block was gone and one page travelled. The selection now survives the press, exactly as it does in File Explorer.
- **A dropped block lost its selection**, so a second drag meant selecting it all over again.
- **Dropping pages where they already were rebuilt the document anyway** — select everything, drag anywhere, and the file was rewritten to produce the identical order, costing every unsaved annotation for nothing.


## Also in this release

- **The bundled PDF engine is now PDFium 154.0.8035**, up from a September 2023 build. This is what makes real redaction possible: the old engine could find content inside a page's embedded objects but not remove it. Rendering and OCR are unaffected.
- **A new application icon.** The old one was the Doodle Project logo at full bleed, so every window and Alt-Tab entry read as the company rather than the app. It is now a document carrying that same mark. The `.pdf` file-association icon is unchanged — PDFs should still look like PDFs.
- **Add/Remove Programs reports the installed size, install date, and links to the project and issue tracker.**
- **`/S`, `/quiet`, `/verysilent` and `--silent` are accepted as synonyms for `/install /silent`**, so the switch most deployment tooling reaches for by habit now works.
- **Fixed:** `TDPdf.exe /silent` tried to open a file literally named `/silent` instead of installing.
- **Releases are signed through Azure Artifact Signing**, so the signature chains to a publicly trusted root rather than one only managed machines recognise. This takes effect once the signing credentials are in place; until then the build falls back to the previous certificate and says so plainly rather than quietly shipping something different.

## Installing

One self-contained `TDPdf.exe`. No runtime to install. Run it from anywhere and it offers to install itself per-user, or to stay portable.

Managed fleets are updated through Intune automatically; nothing to do.
